This article highlights the issue of Google Play Store blocking AuroraStore, which impacts users of privacy-focused Android distributions like GrapheneOS, LineageOS, and /e/OS. The Hacker News discussion was mixed, with some commenters appreciating AuroraStore for its lack of toxicity, absence of dark patterns, and ability to function without a Google account. Many users praised its utility for degoogled or privacy-conscious setups, especially for managing apps on devices without Google services. At the same time, several commenters raised concerns about the instability of AuroraStore, noting that it frequently breaks or fails to update apps, leaving users with outdated software. Others criticized the title for being overly editorialized, pointing out that the cause of the blockage was unclear and not definitively tied to Google’s actions. Some users also highlighted the lack of a straightforward, official way to install Android apps without a Google account, framing it as a fundamental limitation of the Android ecosystem. Overall, the discussion suggests that while AuroraStore is valued for its privacy and usability in certain contexts, its reliability and the broader challenges of degoogled Android usage remain significant issues.
